verses.kjv: Now these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.
verses.modern: These are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob, each with his household:

verses.kjv: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
verses.modern: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,

verses.kjv: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
verses.modern: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,

verses.kjv: Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
verses.modern: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

verses.kjv: And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.
verses.modern: All the descendants of Jacob were seventy persons; Joseph was already in Egypt.

verses.kjv: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.
verses.modern: Then Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.
verses.modern: But the children of Israel were fruitful and increased greatly; they multiplied and grew greatly strong, so that the land was filled with them.

verses.kjv: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.
verses.modern: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.

verses.kjv: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:
verses.modern: he said to his people, 'Look, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.

verses.kjv: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.
verses.modern: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, lest they multiply, and if war breaks out, they join our enemies and fight against us and escape from the land.'

verses.kjv: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.
verses.modern: So they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with heavy burdens. And they built for Pharaoh the store cities Pithom and Raamses.

verses.kjv: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.
verses.modern: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and spread. And the Egyptians were in dread of the children of Israel.

verses.kjv: And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour:
verses.modern: So the Egyptians made the children of Israel serve with harshness.

verses.kjv: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
verses.modern: They made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar and brick and in all kinds of work in the fields. In all their work they ruthlessly made them serve.

verses.kjv: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:
verses.modern: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah,

verses.kjv: And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
verses.modern: 'When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women and see them on the birthstool, if it is a son, you shall kill him, but if it is a daughter, she shall live.'

verses.kjv: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.
verses.modern: But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but let the male children live.

verses.kjv: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?
verses.modern: So the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, 'Why have you done this, and let the male children live?'

verses.kjv: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them.
verses.modern: The midwives said to Pharaoh, 'Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife comes to them.'

verses.kjv: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.
verses.modern: So God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.
verses.modern: because the midwives feared God, He gave them households of their own.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
verses.modern: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, 'Every son that is born to the Hebrews you shall cast into the Nile, but every daughter you shall let live.'

chapters.summary: The children of Israel multiplied greatly in Egypt after Joseph's death until a new Pharaoh who did not know Joseph arose and enslaved them with bitter labor, forcing them to build the store cities of Pithom and Raamses. When oppression failed to slow their growth, Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill every newborn son, but they feared God and disobeyed; finally Pharaoh commanded all his people to cast every Hebrew son into the Nile.

verses.kjv: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.
verses.modern: Now a man of the house of Levi went and took as his wife a daughter of Levi.

verses.kjv: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.
verses.modern: The woman conceived and bore a son, and when she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him three months.

verses.kjv: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.
verses.modern: When she could hide him no longer, she took for him a basket made of bulrushes and daubed it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child in it and placed it among the reeds by the river bank.

verses.kjv: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.
verses.modern: his sister stood at a distance to know what would be done to him.

verses.kjv: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river's side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.
verses.modern: Now the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the river, while her attendants walked beside the river. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her servant woman to fetch it.

verses.kjv: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children.
verses.modern: When she opened it, she saw the child, and the baby was crying. She took pity on him and said, 'This is one of the Hebrews' children.'

verses.kjv: Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?
verses.modern: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, 'Shall I go and call you a nurse from the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?'

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child's mother.
verses.modern: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, 'Go.' So the girl went and called the child's mother.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh's daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the women took the child, and nursed it.
verses.modern: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, 'Take this child away and nurse him for me. I will give you your wages.' So the woman took the child and nursed him.

verses.kjv: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
verses.modern: When the child grew up, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter. He became her son. She named him Moses, saying, 'Because I drew him out of the water.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.
verses.modern: One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers and looked on their burdens. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his brothers.

verses.kjv: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
verses.modern: He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

verses.kjv: And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
verses.modern: The next day he went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He said to the man in the wrong, 'Why do you strike your companion?'

verses.kjv: And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.
verses.modern: The man said, 'Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?' Then Moses was afraid and said, 'Surely the thing is known.'

verses.kjv: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
verses.modern: When Pharaoh heard of it, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian. He sat down by a well.

verses.kjv: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
verses.modern: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.

verses.kjv: And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
verses.modern: The shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and saved them, and watered their flock.

verses.kjv: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to day?
verses.modern: When they came home to their father Reuel, he said, 'How is it that you have come so soon today?'

verses.kjv: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.
verses.modern: They said, 'An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds and even drew water for us and watered the flock.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that ye have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.
verses.modern: He said to his daughters, 'Then where is he? Why have you left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.'

verses.kjv: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
verses.modern: Moses was content to dwell with the man. He gave Moses his daughter Zipporah.

verses.kjv: And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.
verses.modern: She gave birth to a son. He called his name Gershom, for he said, 'I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.
verses.modern: During those many days the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel groaned because of their slavery and cried out for help. Their cry for rescue from slavery came up to God.

verses.kjv: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
verses.modern: God heard their groaning. God remembered His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

verses.kjv: And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.
verses.modern: God saw the children of Israel. God knew.

chapters.summary: A Levite woman hid her infant son three months, then placed him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile; Pharaoh's daughter found the child, named him Moses, and raised him in the palace. As an adult Moses killed an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, and when the deed became known he fled to Midian, where he married Zipporah the daughter of Reuel. Meanwhile God heard the groaning of Israel in their bondage and remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

verses.kjv: Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb.
verses.modern: Now Moses was keeping the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led his flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

verses.kjv: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
verses.modern: the angel of the LORD appeared to Him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush. He looked, and the bush was burning, yet it was not consumed.

verses.kjv: And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
verses.modern: Moses said, 'I will turn aside to see this great sight, why the bush is not burned.'

verses.kjv: And when the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.
verses.modern: When the LORD saw that He turned aside to see, God called to Him out of the bush, 'Moses, Moses!' And he said, 'Here I am.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
verses.modern: Then He said, 'Do not come near; take Your sandals off Your feet, for the place on which You are standing is holy ground.'

verses.kjv: Moreover he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.
verses.modern: he said, 'I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' And Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;
verses.modern: Then the LORD said, 'I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters. I know their sorrows,

verses.kjv: And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.modern: I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land to a good and broad land, a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

verses.kjv: Now therefore, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: and I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.
verses.modern: now, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me. I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.

verses.kjv: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
verses.modern: Come, I will send you to Pharaoh that you may bring my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
verses.modern: But Moses said to God, 'Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?'

verses.kjv: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.
verses.modern: He said, 'I will be with you, and this shall be the sign for you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say unto them?
verses.modern: Then Moses said to God, 'If I come to the children of Israel and say to them, The God of your fathers has sent me to you. They ask me, What is His name? what shall I say to them?'

verses.kjv: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.
verses.modern: God said to Moses, 'I AM THAT I AM.' And he said, 'Say this to the children of Israel: I AM has sent me to you.'

verses.kjv: And God said moreover unto Moses, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
verses.modern: God also said to Moses, 'Say this to the children of Israel: The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This is my name forever, and thus I am to be remembered throughout all generations.

verses.kjv: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, appeared unto me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt:
verses.modern: Go and gather the elders of Israel together and say to them, The LORD, the God of Your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, I have observed You and what has been done to You in Egypt,

verses.kjv: And I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt unto the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.modern: I promise that I will bring You up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey.

verses.kjv: And they shall hearken to thy voice: and thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye shall say unto him, The LORD God of the Hebrews hath met with us: and now let us go, we beseech thee, three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.
verses.modern: they will listen to Your voice, and You and the elders of Israel shall go to the king of Egypt and say to him, The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. And now, please let us go a three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.

verses.kjv: And I am sure that the king of Egypt will not let you go, no, not by a mighty hand.
verses.modern: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless compelled by a mighty hand.

verses.kjv: And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.
verses.modern: So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders that I will do in it; after that he will let you go.

verses.kjv: And I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty:
verses.modern: I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that when you go, you shall not go empty.

verses.kjv: But every woman shall borrow of her neighbour, and of her that sojourneth in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment: and ye shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters; and ye shall spoil the Egyptians.
verses.modern: Each woman shall ask of her neighbor, and any woman who lives in her house, for silver and gold jewelry, and for clothing. You shall put them on your sons and on your daughters. So you shall plunder the Egyptians.'

chapters.summary: While tending Jethro's flock near Horeb, Moses saw a bush burning with fire that was not consumed; God spoke from the bush, revealing himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and commissioned Moses to deliver Israel from Egypt. When Moses asked God's name, God answered "I AM THAT I AM" and promised to bring the people out to a land flowing with milk and honey, warning that Pharaoh would not let them go except by a mighty hand.

verses.kjv: And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice: for they will say, The LORD hath not appeared unto thee.
verses.modern: Then Moses answered, 'But they will not believe me or listen to my voice, for they will say, The LORD did not appear to You.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto him, What is that in thine hand? And he said, A rod.
verses.modern: The LORD said to Him, 'What is that in Your hand?' He said, 'A staff.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
verses.modern: he said, 'Throw it on the ground.' So he threw it on the ground. It became a serpent, and Moses ran from it.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Put forth thine hand, and take it by the tail. And he put forth his hand, and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand:
verses.modern: But the LORD said to Moses, 'Put out your hand and catch it by the tail.' So He put out His hand and caught it. It became a staff in His hand,

verses.kjv: That they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.
verses.modern: 'that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said furthermore unto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous as snow.
verses.modern: The LORD said to Him again, 'Put Your hand inside Your cloak.' And He put His hand inside His cloak, and when He took it out, His hand was leprous like snow.

verses.kjv: And he said, Put thine hand into thy bosom again. And he put his hand into his bosom again; and plucked it out of his bosom, and, behold, it was turned again as his other flesh.
verses.modern: Then God said, 'Put Your hand back inside Your cloak.' So He put His hand back inside His cloak, and when He took it out, it was restored like the rest of His flesh.

verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
verses.modern: 'If they will not believe You or listen to the first sign, they may believe the latter sign.

verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe also these two signs, neither hearken unto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river, and pour it upon the dry land: and the water which thou takest out of the river shall become blood upon the dry land.
verses.modern: If they will not believe even these two signs or listen to Your voice, You shall take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground, and the water that You shall take from the Nile will become blood on the dry ground.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto the LORD, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
verses.modern: But Moses said to the LORD, 'Oh, my Lord, I am not eloquent, either in the past or since You have spoken to Your servant. But I am slow of speech and of tongue.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto him, Who hath made man's mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the LORD?
verses.modern: Then the LORD said to Him, 'Who has made man's mouth? Who makes Him mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?

verses.kjv: Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.
verses.modern: Now therefore go. I will be with Your mouth and teach You what You shall speak.'

verses.kjv: And he said, O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.
verses.modern: But He said, 'Oh, my Lord, please send someone else.'

verses.kjv: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
verses.modern: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses and he said, 'Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. He is coming out to meet You, and when He sees You, He will be glad in His heart.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt speak unto him, and put words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.
verses.modern: You shall speak to Him and put the words in His mouth. I will be with Your mouth and with His mouth and will teach You both what You shall do.

verses.kjv: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
verses.modern: He shall speak for You to the people. He shall be your mouth, and you shall be as God to Him.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs.
verses.modern: take in Your hand this staff, with which You shall do the signs.'

verses.kjv: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father in law, and said unto him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren which are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.
verses.modern: Moses went back to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him, 'Please let me go back to my brothers in Egypt to see whether they are still alive.' And Jethro said to Moses, 'Go in peace.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.
verses.modern: the LORD said to Moses in Midian, 'Go back to Egypt, for all the men who were seeking your life are dead.'

verses.kjv: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of God in his hand.
verses.modern: So Moses took his wife and his sons and had them ride on a donkey, and went back to the land of Egypt. And Moses took the staff of God in His hand.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, When thou goest to return into Egypt, see that thou do all those wonders before Pharaoh, which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go.
verses.modern: the LORD said to Moses, 'When you go back to Egypt, see that you do before Pharaoh all the miracles that I have put in your power. But I will harden His heart, so that He will not let the people go.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my son, even my firstborn:
verses.modern: Then You shall say to Pharaoh, Thus says the LORD, Israel is my firstborn son,

verses.kjv: And I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.
verses.modern: I say to You, Let my son go that He may serve me. If You refuse to let Him go, I will kill Your firstborn son.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him.
verses.modern: At a lodging place on the way the LORD met Him and sought to put Him to death.

verses.kjv: Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.
verses.modern: Then Zipporah took a flint and cut off her son's foreskin and cast it at His feet and said, 'Surely a bloody husband You are to me!'

verses.kjv: So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.
verses.modern: So He let Him alone. Then she said, 'A bloody husband,' because of the circumcision.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him in the mount of God, and kissed him.
verses.modern: The LORD said to Aaron, 'Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.' So he went and met him at the mountain of God and kissed Him.

verses.kjv: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD who had sent him, and all the signs which he had commanded him.
verses.modern: Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD Who had sent Him, and all the signs that He had commanded Him.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel:
verses.modern: Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.

verses.kjv: And Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.
verses.modern: Aaron spoke all the words that the LORD had spoken to Moses and did the signs in the sight of the people.

verses.kjv: And the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.
verses.modern: the people believed, and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel and that He had seen their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshiped.

chapters.summary: God gave Moses three signs to prove his authority — the staff turned serpent, the leprous hand, and water turned to blood — and when Moses protested that he was slow of speech, the LORD angrily appointed Aaron as his spokesman. Moses returned to Egypt with his family; on the way the LORD sought to kill him until Zipporah circumcised their son. Aaron met Moses at the mountain of God, and together they gathered Israel's elders, performed the signs, and the people believed and worshiped.

verses.kjv: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.
verses.modern: Afterward Moses and Aaron went and said to Pharaoh, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.'

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go.
verses.modern: But Pharaoh said, 'Who is the LORD, that I should obey His voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and moreover, I will not let Israel go.'

verses.kjv: And they said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days' journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto the LORD our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.
verses.modern: Then they said, 'The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go a three days' journey into the wilderness that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God, lest He fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword.'

verses.kjv: And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.
verses.modern: But the king of Egypt said to them, 'Moses and Aaron, why do you take the people away from their work? Get back to your burdens.'

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh said, Behold, the people of the land now are many, and ye make them rest from their burdens.
verses.modern: Pharaoh said, ' the people of the land are now many, and you make them rest from their burdens.'

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh commanded the same day the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,
verses.modern: The same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their foremen,

verses.kjv: Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.
verses.modern: 'You shall no longer give the people straw to make bricks, as before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.

verses.kjv: And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.
verses.modern: But the number of bricks that they made in the past you shall impose on them; you shall not reduce it, for they are idle. That is why they cry, Let us go and offer sacrifice to our God.

verses.kjv: Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words.
verses.modern: Let heavier work be laid on the men, that they may labor at it and pay no regard to lying words.'

verses.kjv: And the taskmasters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spake to the people, saying, Thus saith Pharaoh, I will not give you straw.
verses.modern: So the taskmasters and the foremen of the people went out and said to the people, 'Thus says Pharaoh, I will not give you straw.

verses.kjv: Go ye, get you straw where ye can find it: yet not ought of your work shall be diminished.
verses.modern: Go and get your straw yourselves wherever you can find it, but your work will not be reduced in the least.'

verses.kjv: So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble instead of straw.
verses.modern: So the people were scattered throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

verses.kjv: And the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw.
verses.modern: The taskmasters were urgent, saying, 'Complete your work, your daily task each day, as when there was straw.'

verses.kjv: And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?
verses.modern: the foremen of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten and were asked, 'Why have you not done all your work of making bricks today and yesterday, as in the past?'

verses.kjv: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants?
verses.modern: Then the foremen of the children of Israel came and cried to Pharaoh, 'Why do you treat your servants like this?

verses.kjv: There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people.
verses.modern: No straw is given to your servants, yet they say to us, Make bricks! And your servants are beaten, but the fault is in your own people.'

verses.kjv: But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD.
verses.modern: But He said, 'You are idle, You are idle; that is why You say, Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.

verses.kjv: Go therefore now, and work; for there shall no straw be given you, yet shall ye deliver the tale of bricks.
verses.modern: Go now and work. No straw will be given You, but You must still deliver the same number of bricks.'

verses.kjv: And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in evil case, after it was said, Ye shall not minish ought from your bricks of your daily task.
verses.modern: The foremen of the children of Israel saw that they were in trouble when they said, 'You shall by no means reduce Your number of bricks, Your daily task each day.'

verses.kjv: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh:
verses.modern: They met Moses and Aaron, who were waiting for them, as they came out from Pharaoh.

verses.kjv: And they said unto them, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.
verses.modern: they said to them, 'The LORD look on You and judge, because You have made us stink in the sight of Pharaoh and his servants, and have put a sword in their hand to kill us.'

verses.kjv: And Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me?
verses.modern: Then Moses turned to the LORD and said, 'O Lord, why have You done evil to this people? Why did You ever send me?

verses.kjv: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.
verses.modern: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has done evil to this people, and you have not delivered your people at all.'

chapters.summary: Moses and Aaron told Pharaoh to let Israel go, but Pharaoh refused and instead increased the people's burden, requiring them to gather their own straw while maintaining the same quota of bricks. The Israelite foremen were beaten when they could not meet the demand, and they blamed Moses and Aaron for making things worse. Moses cried out to the LORD, asking why he had brought more evil upon the people instead of delivering them.

verses.kjv: Then the LORD said unto Moses, Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh: for with a strong hand shall he let them go, and with a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land.
verses.modern: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand he will send them out, and with a strong hand He will drive them out of His land.'

verses.kjv: And God spake unto Moses, and said unto him, I am the LORD:
verses.modern: God spoke to Moses and said to him, 'I am the LORD.

verses.kjv: And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, but by my name JEHOVAH was I not known to them.
verses.modern: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty, but by my name JEHOVAH was I not known to them.

verses.kjv: And I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their pilgrimage, wherein they were strangers.
verses.modern: I also established my covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan, the land in which they lived as sojourners.

verses.kjv: And I have also heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage; and I have remembered my covenant.
verses.modern: Moreover, I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians hold as slaves. I have remembered my covenant.

verses.kjv: Wherefore say unto the children of Israel, I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with a stretched out arm, and with great judgments:
verses.modern: Say therefore to the children of Israel, I am the LORD. I will bring You out from under the burdens of the Egyptians. I will deliver You from slavery to them. I will redeem You with an outstretched arm and with great acts of judgment.

verses.kjv: And I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God: and ye shall know that I am the LORD your God, which bringeth you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
verses.modern: I will take You to be my people. I will be Your God, and You shall know that I am the LORD Your God, Who has brought You out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.

verses.kjv: And I will bring you in unto the land, concerning the which I did swear to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for an heritage: I am the LORD.
verses.modern: I will bring You into the land that I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. I will give it to you for a possession. I am the LORD.'

verses.kjv: And Moses spake so unto the children of Israel: but they hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
verses.modern: Moses spoke thus to the children of Israel. But they did not listen to Moses, because of their broken spirit and harsh slavery.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.modern: So the LORD said to Moses,

verses.kjv: Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.modern: 'Go in, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the children of Israel go out of his land.'

verses.kjv: And Moses spake before the LORD, saying, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips?
verses.modern: But Moses said to the LORD, ' the children of Israel have not listened to me. How then shall Pharaoh listen to me, for I am of uncircumcised lips?'

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, and gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: But the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge about the children of Israel and about Pharaoh king of Egypt: to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: These be the heads of their fathers' houses: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel; Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi: these be the families of Reuben.
verses.modern: These are the heads of their fathers' houses: the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the clans of Reuben.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman: these are the families of Simeon.
verses.modern: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the clans of Simeon.

verses.kjv: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations; Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari: and the years of the life of Levi were an hundred thirty and seven years.
verses.modern: These are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, the years of the life of Levi being 137 years.

verses.kjv: The sons of Gershon; Libni, and Shimi, according to their families.
verses.modern: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, by their clans.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath were an hundred thirty and three years.
verses.modern: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, the years of the life of Kohath being 133 years.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Merari; Mahali and Mushi: these are the families of Levi according to their generations.
verses.modern: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites according to their generations.

verses.kjv: And Amram took him Jochebed his father's sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were an hundred and thirty and seven years.
verses.modern: Amram took as his wife Jochebed his father's sister. She bore him Aaron and Moses, the years of the life of Amram being 137 years.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Izhar; Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
verses.modern: The sons of Izhar: Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Uzziel; Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Zithri.
verses.modern: The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.

verses.kjv: And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.modern: Aaron took as his wife Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon. She bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Korah; Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these are the families of the Korhites.
verses.modern: The sons of Korah: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the clans of the Korahites.

verses.kjv: And Eleazar Aaron's son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas: these are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their families.
verses.modern: Eleazar, Aaron's son, took as his wife one of the daughters of Putiel. She bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites by their clans.

verses.kjv: These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom the LORD said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their armies.
verses.modern: These are the Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD said, 'Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt by their hosts.'

verses.kjv: These are they which spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt: these are that Moses and Aaron.
verses.modern: It was they who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt about bringing out the children of Israel from Egypt — this Moses and this Aaron.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass on the day when the LORD spake unto Moses in the land of Egypt,
verses.modern: On the day when the LORD spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,

verses.kjv: That the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, I am the LORD: speak thou unto Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I say unto thee.
verses.modern: the LORD said to Moses, 'I am the LORD. Tell Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I say to you.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said before the LORD, Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh hearken unto me?
verses.modern: But Moses said to the LORD, ' I am of uncircumcised lips. How will Pharaoh listen to me?'

chapters.summary: The LORD reassured Moses, revealing his name JEHOVAH and renewing his covenant promises to bring Israel out of Egypt with great judgments and give them the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The genealogy of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi is given, tracing the Levitical line through Kohath and Amram to Moses and Aaron, and through Aaron to his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. The LORD commanded Moses and Aaron again to go to Pharaoh despite Moses' protest that he was of uncircumcised lips.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, See, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.
verses.modern: the LORD said to Moses, 'See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron shall be your prophet.

verses.kjv: Thou shalt speak all that I command thee: and Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he send the children of Israel out of his land.
verses.modern: You shall speak all that I command you, and your brother Aaron shall tell Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of his land.

verses.kjv: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and though I multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,

verses.kjv: But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
verses.modern: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt and bring my hosts, my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great acts of judgment.

verses.kjv: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I stretch forth mine hand upon Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.
verses.modern: The Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring out the children of Israel from among them.'

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron did as the LORD commanded them, so did they.
verses.modern: Moses and Aaron did so; they did just as the LORD commanded them.

verses.kjv: And Moses was fourscore years old, and Aaron fourscore and three years old, when they spake unto Pharaoh.
verses.modern: Now Moses was 80 years old, and Aaron 83 years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
verses.modern: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

verses.kjv: When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Shew a miracle for you: then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent.
verses.modern: 'When Pharaoh says to you, Prove yourselves by working a miracle, then you shall say to Aaron, Take your staff and cast it down before Pharaoh, that it may become a serpent.'

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the LORD had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
verses.modern: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD commanded. Aaron cast down his staff before Pharaoh and his servants. It became a serpent.

verses.kjv: Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments.
verses.modern: Then Pharaoh summoned the wise men and the sorcerers. They, the magicians of Egypt, also did the same by their secret arts.

verses.kjv: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.
verses.modern: For each man cast down his staff. They became serpents. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.

verses.kjv: And he hardened Pharaoh's heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said.
verses.modern: Still Pharaoh's heart was hardened. He would not listen to them, as the LORD had said.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Pharaoh's heart is hardened, he refuseth to let the people go.
verses.modern: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Pharaoh's heart is hardened; he refuses to let the people go.

verses.kjv: Get thee unto Pharaoh in the morning; lo, he goeth out unto the water; and thou shalt stand by the river's brink against he come; and the rod which was turned to a serpent shalt thou take in thine hand.
verses.modern: Go to Pharaoh in the morning, as he is going out to the water. Stand on the bank of the Nile to meet him, and take in your hand the staff that turned into a serpent.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt say unto him, The LORD God of the Hebrews hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto thou wouldest not hear.
verses.modern: you shall say to Him, The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to You, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness. But so far, You have not obeyed.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, In this thou shalt know that I am the LORD: behold, I will smite with the rod that is in mine hand upon the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.
verses.modern: Thus says the LORD, By this You shall know that I am the LORD: with the staff that is in my hand I will strike the water that is in the Nile. It shall turn into blood.

verses.kjv: And the fish that is in the river shall die, and the river shall stink; and the Egyptians shall lothe to drink of the water of the river.
verses.modern: The fish in the Nile shall die, and the Nile will stink, and the Egyptians will grow weary of drinking water from the Nile.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and that there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone.
verses.modern: the LORD said to Moses, 'Say to Aaron, Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, their canals, their ponds, and all their pools of water, so that they may become blood, and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, even in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.'

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron did so, as the LORD commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
verses.modern: Moses and Aaron did as the LORD commanded. In the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants he lifted up the staff and struck the water in the Nile. All the water in the Nile turned into blood.

verses.kjv: And the fish that was in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river; and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: the fish in the Nile died, and the Nile stank, so that the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile. There was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, neither did he hearken unto them; as the LORD had said.
verses.modern: But the magicians of Egypt did the same by their secret arts. So Pharaoh's heart remained hardened. He would not listen to them, as the LORD had said.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, neither did he set his heart to this also.
verses.modern: Pharaoh turned and went into his house. He did not take even this to heart.

verses.kjv: And all the Egyptians digged round about the river for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the river.
verses.modern: all the Egyptians dug along the Nile for water to drink, for they could not drink the water of the Nile.

verses.kjv: And seven days were fulfilled, after that the LORD had smitten the river.
verses.modern: Seven full days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.

chapters.summary: The LORD made Moses as God to Pharaoh and Aaron his prophet, warning that he would harden Pharaoh's heart and multiply his signs in Egypt. Aaron's staff became a serpent before Pharaoh and swallowed the staffs of the Egyptian magicians, but Pharaoh's heart remained hard. The LORD sent the first plague: Aaron struck the Nile with his staff and all the water turned to blood, killing the fish and making the river stink for seven days.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, Go unto Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.modern: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, Thus says the LORD, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.kjv: And if thou refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs:
verses.modern: But if You refuse to let them go, I will plague all Your country with frogs.

verses.kjv: And the river shall bring forth frogs abundantly, which shall go up and come into thine house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneadingtroughs:
verses.modern: The Nile shall swarm with frogs that shall come up into Your house and into Your bedroom and on Your bed and into the houses of Your servants and Your people, and into Your ovens and Your kneading bowls.

verses.kjv: And the frogs shall come up both on thee, and upon thy people, and upon all thy servants.
verses.modern: The frogs shall come up on You and on Your people and on all Your servants.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thine hand with thy rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: the LORD said to Moses, 'Say to Aaron, Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals and over the pools, and make frogs come up on the land of Egypt!'

verses.kjv: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And the magicians did so with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.
verses.modern: But the magicians did the same by their secret arts and made frogs come up on the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Intreat the LORD, that he may take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may do sacrifice unto the LORD.
verses.modern: Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, 'Plead with the LORD to take away the frogs from me and from my people. I will let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto Pharaoh, Glory over me: when shall I intreat for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, to destroy the frogs from thee and thy houses, that they may remain in the river only?
verses.modern: Moses said to Pharaoh, 'Have the honor of telling me when I am to plead for you and your servants and your people, that the frogs be cut off from you and your houses and be left only in the Nile.'

verses.kjv: And he said, To morrow. And he said, Be it according to thy word: that thou mayest know that there is none like unto the LORD our God.
verses.modern: he said, 'Tomorrow.' Moses said, 'Be it as you say, so that you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God.

verses.kjv: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; they shall remain in the river only.
verses.modern: The frogs shall go away from You and Your houses and Your servants and Your people. They shall be left only in the Nile.'

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh: and Moses cried unto the LORD because of the frogs which he had brought against Pharaoh.
verses.modern: So Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried to the LORD about the frogs, as He had agreed with Pharaoh.

verses.kjv: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses; and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the villages, and out of the fields.
verses.modern: the LORD did according to the word of Moses. The frogs died out in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields.

verses.kjv: And they gathered them together upon heaps: and the land stank.
verses.modern: they gathered them together in heaps, and the land stank.
